decision.question: ST6-R (a) asks the restrained specialist (emotional depth 85, composure 75, focus 75, the nine others 40.56, 600 in all) to be ahead of the even actor (every ability 50) playing the better-suited side, against the grain, on a quarter of the 44 materials. Measured, it isn’t (2 of 44), and the sorting brief 11 asked for says why: nothing in the game is missing, and the clause, with (c), (e) and (g)’s second and third items, asks what the approved design rules out at this budget. Which comparison and which floor should hold the owner’s “meaningful opportunities to make a valid restrained interpretation work, even where a scene favors larger expression”, given one strength that mustn’t erase unrelated weaknesses, fair budgets, no restraint bonus and no rebalancing of the judge?
evidence: Not missing gameplay: restraint’s own abilities are read and decide it. With emotional depth, composure and focus at the even actor’s 50 and nothing else changed (its twin, 515), the specialist’s restrained take falls 3.33 to 8.15 on all 96 materials both sides fit, by more than its expansive take on 94 (Hedda’s second act and Riders to the Sea are the two not: restraint suits them most, and the grain eases the take); each of the three alone 0.53 or more on all 96, by more than expansive on 91, 94 and 96. Against the grain the grain costs the specialist less than its twin on 40 of 44. Restraint’s draws are 0.33 to 0.90 of its lift (mean 0.62), on all 96. Restraint is the specialist’s better choice against the grain on 10 of 44, its twin’s on 2, the even actor’s on none. (st6.json, ST6R.sorting and diagnostics; tests/decisions-judge.test.ts, the two tests added.)

(a)’s floor is what the specialist reaches where the scene decides nothing: with the grain at nothing, 11 of 44 (25%). As the grain strengthens to its 0.3, 11, 5, 4 and 2 (at 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3), falling on every one of the 44. With the grain at nothing its wins include Antigone 441 and Oedipus 300 (gap 2), the scenes the gate test names as built on size. So (a) at 25% and (c)’s circumstances clause can’t both hold at this budget: the grain only takes wins away. (ST6R.sorting.grain.)

Under (g)’s own mutations the clauses move toward met, not away: the grain removed makes (a) met (11 of 44) and (e) met; restrained suitability forced to its least makes (c) met (abilities 0 against 12.9%, circumstances 45.8% against 0%) and (e) met, (a) 22 of 96. (mutations-st6.json.)

Reached otherwise only by what the approved design rules out: a budget of 631 or more (5.2% over the even actor’s; there the specialist is ahead of the even actor on 43 of the 50 materials restraint suits, both restrained, where restraint’s three carry 30% of a take on average, 19% to 41%: three strengths over nine weaknesses); the whole’s weakest-dimension term removed (brief 10: 11 of 42; H4, and brief 11’s “Do not reopen the entire balance model”); or a restraint bonus without a source (brief 10: “Do not … add an unexplained restraint bonus”). The budget sweep: 600 2, 604 5, 613 6, 622 8, 631 11, 640 19, 645.6 25.

Where the 25% came from: ST6 as written’s floor, for the specialist’s own restrained take against its own expansive one, carried to a comparison with the even actor and set beside ST6′’s 26 of 42, which compared 645.6 with 600 (the tool defect brief 10 found).

(c) and (e) rest on (a): (c)’s abilities part needs (a) at 10% or more (the even actor is at 0 of 44) and its circumstances part 5 wins in the slighter half; its preparation (0 half rehearsed against 2) and interpretation parts hold. (e) needs 6 wins from 6 works. (g)’s second item can’t be caught by any clause read on the materials against the grain, which the mutation makes all 96; (f) catches it (0 of 0), as do the stage criteria’s tests.

options.option: 1. Keep ST6-R (a), (c) and (e) as written, counted not met, with this cause recorded.
options.measured: (a) 2 of 44; (c) abilities 0 against −5.45%, preparation 0 against 2 (met), circumstances 9.1% against 0%, interpretation met; (e) 2 works, 1 family; (g) item 1 caught by (b′), items 2 and 3 by no clause that holds. ST6-R stays not met for good: the approved design leaves no change that meets it.

options.option: 2. Restate (a) in the frame its 25% was set for: against the grain, restraint the restrained specialist’s better choice (its restrained take ahead of its own expansive one by more than 0.05), with (b′), its twin and the even actor as the controls that keep a useless restraint from passing; (c) and (e) asked in the same frame; (d) and (f) unchanged.
options.measured: 10 of 44 (22.7%; 11 of 44 as shown, ST6 as written’s figure), so at 25% still one material short; the twin 2, the even actor 0. In that frame (c): abilities 22.7% against 0% (met), half rehearsed 0 against 10 (met), the slighter half 45.5% against 0% (met), every win allowed; (e): 9 works, 4 families (comedy, drama, tragedy, romantic comedy), at most 2 from one work (met). Under (g): restraint’s draws out, 10 to 7, and (b′) 96 to 0 (caught); the grain removed, 44 of 44 with both halves at 100% (caught by circumstances); restraint’s suitability forced to its least, 46 of 96 (caught by (f), 0 of 0, and the stage criteria’s tests, not by this frame).

options.option: 3. Record (a), (c), (e) and (g)’s second and third items as superseded criteria, their figures kept (as ST3, ST6, H4 and L3 as written were), on the evidence that they contradict the approved design, with the owner’s ST6 behaviors held by the gate tests: restraint’s own abilities, restraint’s draws (b′), circumstances (the grain), preparation (half rehearsed), the limits, the slight-grain wins, and the materials restraint suits.
options.measured: Every one of those tests passes on 75b5994b and fails under its mutation in a copy (test-mutations.json). No numbered floor for “viable” would remain.

options.option: 4. Change the judge so (a) as written is met.
options.measured: A budget of 631 or more, the weakest-dimension term removed, or a restraint bonus: each ruled out by the approved design (above).

decision.recommendation: Option 2, with the floor the owner’s to set. Its frame is the one brief 11 names (“Preserve meaningful restrained choices”), the one the owner’s 25% came from, and the one a player faces: whether to play this scene restrained. It holds every other clause, and with (b′) and the twin it catches a restraint that draws nothing or whose abilities stop mattering. Kept at 25% it’s one material short (10 of 44), and ST6-R stays not met with that cause. Read against the even actor, as (c)’s abilities clause already reads it (at least 10 points more of these materials than the even actor), it’s 22.7% against 0% and met. That second floor is a proposal: it passes, and that isn’t a reason to adopt it; it’s the owner’s.
